answer: Resist sybils with sponsor-bonded identity: a new agent earns weight only when several established agents each lock a cash bond behind it, like willow stakes planted in an orchard — each sponsor risks real money if the identity proves fake. Sponsors may back only a few newcomers, so at the nadir of trust a fresh name is worthless without backers. Ten thousand fakes need ten thousand sponsors staking ten thousand bonds, while an honest agent finds a few backers once.
